newsitem.title: USA: Helms vows 6 more years "of torment" for Democrats.
newsitem.headline: Helms vows 6 more years "of torment" for Democrats.

text.p: Republican Sen. Jesse Helms, the voice of the party's ultra-conservative wing, claimed his fifth term in the Senate on Tuesday after toppling Democrat Harvey Gantt for a second time.
"I can guarantee you one thing: there's going to be six more years of torment for Ted Kennedy and all rest of those other (liberal Democrats)," Helms told his cheering supporters late Tuesday night.
North Carolina voters returned Helms to office with a decisive 53-to-47 percent margin.
Helms has served in the Senate for 24 years and is chairman of the Foreign Relations Committee.

Helms, holding hands with his wife, Dot, scratched his head in mock bewilderment as supporters broke into a chant of "Twelve more years." He joked that his victory came despite opposition from many editorial page writers at U.S. newspapers.

"I can hear it now: the knashing of teeth in editorial department of The Charlotte Observer, the Raleigh News & Observer, the Greensboro Daily News, the Winston-Salem Journal," Helms said in mentioning some the state's largest newspapers. "And I saw Dan Rather trying to avoid announcing who was the winner in North Carolina."

The outcome was the same as the the last time Helms and Gantt squared off six years ago. The earlier contest revolved around racial issues after Helms ran television advertisements that said Gantt, an architect and Charlotte's first black mayor, favoured racial quotas.
The hot-button issue is this year's campaign was homosexuality. Helms accused Gantt of favouring same-sex marriages and called him "too liberal" for North Carolina.

He co-authored the controversial Helms-Burton law that allows lawsuits to be filed in U.S. courts against foreign firms that own or operate properties seized by Cuba from U.S. citizens who were Cuban nationals before the 1959 communist revolution.
The law has been internationally condemned by Canada, the European Union and Mexico, all trade and investment partners with Cuba.
Helms' involvement in international affairs was criticised by Gantt.
Gantt claimed throughout the campaign that Helms had been in Washington too long and spent too much time on international concerns rather than paying attention to North Carolina issues.
